parsed.explanation: Traveller-facing exposures are substantial and documented. Strip-searching by birth sex (transport police, interim) and biological-sex search rules in custody and stop-and-search (regional police) are universal-exposure measures reaching any visibly trans visitor. Prison placement by birth sex is contested but government defends individual risk assessments, and the top court ruling excludes GRC holders from 'sex' for equality purposes, affecting single-sex services. A documented hospital ward-exclusion case with death shows real care-access harm, though it concerns a resident and is a single case. Hate-crime protection on gender identity exists only in some regions. Offsets: no criminalisation of gender identity, medical access formally available, equality-law protection from gender-reassignment discrimination retained, and a tolerant-leaning general public. Overall Elevated Risk, with the evidence of hostile state policy outweighing the formal protections.
